source_caption:
Season 4 finale of The Sopranos "Whitecaps" features what is universally recognized as the greatest domestic dispute in prestige television drama history. The sequence is so visceral and emotionally exhausting that it famously earned both James Gandolfini and Edie Falco lead acting Primetime Emmy Awards in the same year a legendary feat fueled by their unmatched, terrifyingly authentic chemistry. Grounded by a towering James Gandolfini acting performance and Falco’s absolute force-of-nature response, this scene proved that the show's true heart wasn't the mob violence, but the slow, agonizing decay of the American dream within the Soprano household.

source_details.title: Whitecaps
source_details.synopsis: "Whitecaps" is the 52nd episode of the HBO television series The Sopranos, and the 13th and final episode of the show's fourth season. Written by the series creator/executive producer David Chase with executive producers Robin Green and Mitchell Burgess, it was directed by longtime series director John Patterson. Originally aired in the U.S. on December 8, 2002, the episode attracted nearly 12.5 million viewers, more in its timeslot than any competing program on broadcast TV. Reviews of the episode were generally positive, and some publications ranked it among the best in the series.
